record.paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
record.original_question: For the no-delay p-periodic stocking equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) + h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic sequence of nonnegative stocking quotas with positive total stocking over one period, each quota ordering has a globally attracting p-periodic solution. If xbar_av is the average of the attracting p-periodic solution for one ordering of the stocking quotas and xhat_av is the average for a permutation of the same quotas, how are xbar_av and xhat_av related?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the scalar discrete-time population model with no delay and periodic stocking
\[ x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n) + h_n, \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \dots, \]
where:
- $f:[0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ is a continuous, positive function such that $x \mapsto x f(x)$ is a (smooth) "contest competition" map: $x f(x)$ is bounded, has a unique positive fixed point, and is such that the unstocked equation $x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_n)$ has a globally attracting positive equilibrium on $(0,\infty)$;
- $\{h_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ is a $p$-periodic sequence of nonnegative real numbers (stocking quotas) with $\sum_{n=0}^{p-1} h_n > 0$.

Under these hypotheses, for every choice (i.e. every cyclic ordering) of the quotas $h_0, h_1, \dots, h_{p-1}$, the equation admits a globally attracting positive $p$-periodic solution $\{x_n^*\}$. Define the temporal average over one period
\[ \bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{n=0}^{p-1} x_n^*. \]

Now let $\sigma$ be any permutation of $\{0,1,\dots,p-1\}$, and let $\hat{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$ denote the analogous average of the globally attracting $p$-periodic solution corresponding to the permuted stocking sequence $h_{\sigma(0)}, h_{\sigma(1)}, \dots, h_{\sigma(p-1)}$.

Determine the relationship between $\bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$ and $\hat{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$. In particular, decide whether $\bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}} = \hat{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$ holds for every permutation $\sigma$, every period $p$, and every admissible map $f$; and if not, characterize the orderings of the quotas that maximize and minimize the average $\bar{x}_{\mathrm{av}}$.
artifact.category_tag: discrete-time population models with periodic stocking
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on discrete contest competition models with periodic stocking. Related work establishes existence and global attractivity of periodic solutions and partial results for small periods (p = 2, 3), but no general result comparing averages across all permutations of stocking quotas appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Paper poses open problems and conjectures about periodic stocking in contest competition models.
status_evidence.claim: The averaging/permutation question is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A Global Attractor in Some Discrete Contest Competition Models with Delay under the Effect of Periodic Stocking
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses periodic stocking, existence and global attractivity of p-periodic solutions, partial results for small p.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses related dynamics but does not resolve the general permutation-of-averages question.
